title: No me hallo
desc: A word for something you have been feeling for a year
setting: You have left a party of thirty people to stand in the patio, and Lucía has come out to find you.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: ¿Y vos qué hacés aquí afuera? ¿Estás bien?
steps.en: And what are you doing out here? Are you all right?

options.es: Sí, pero no me hallo. Así, de repente.
options.en: Yes, but I do not feel right. Just like that, suddenly.
options.feedback: No me hallo is the word and there is no clean English for it. It is not sadness and not anger, it is not finding your place in a room, and everybody here knows it.

options.en: I feel odd. I do not know.
options.feedback: Close, and it will do. Raro is what you say when you have not got the word yet.
Extraño is for a smell or a noise, and said about yourself in a house full of your wife's family it sounds like you feel foreign in it.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Ah, no te hallás. Eso le pasa a todo el mundo, gordo.
steps.en: Ah, you are not finding your place. That happens to everybody, gordo.

options.es: ¿A todo el mundo? Yo creía que era por ser de afuera.
options.en: To everybody? I thought it was from being a foreigner.
options.feedback: It is not. Nicaraguans say no me hallo about a new job, a new barrio, a party full of their own cousins. The word was never about you being foreign.

options.es: Qué bueno saber que no soy solo yo.
options.en: Good to know it is not just me.
options.feedback: True. Ask her when it happens to her and you will get the whole shape of the word.

options.es: A vos no te pasa, seguro.
options.en: It does not happen to you, surely.
options.feedback: It does. Deciding on her behalf that she has never felt it closes the conversation you came out here for.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Claro que sí. Yo no me hallaba en el trabajo nuevo por meses.
steps.en: Of course it does. I did not find my feet in the new job for months.

options.en: And what did you do? Did it go on its own?
options.feedback: Ask, because the answer is usually time and nothing else. Se me quitó is how you say a feeling left you, as though it had come by itself.

options.en: I did not know that about you.
options.feedback: Warm. There was a practical question sitting right there.
She just handed you her own version of it. Telling her it does not count is the wrong thing to do with that.

steps.speaker: Lucía
steps.es: Se me fue solo. Entrá, que ya van a servir.
steps.en: It went on its own. Come in, they are about to serve.

options.es: Ya voy. Dame dos minutos y entro.
options.en: Coming. Give me two minutes and I will come in.
options.feedback: You are not being asked to be cured, only to come back in. Two minutes and the plate is the whole treatment.

options.en: All right, I am coming in.
options.feedback: Fine. Taking the two minutes you actually need is allowed.

options.es: Entrá vos, yo me quedo aquí.
options.en: You go in, I will stay here.
options.feedback: Standing alone in a patio while thirty people eat is how not finding your place turns into being outside it.
